claims.text: Greg Short attributes his three consecutive consumer-product hits (Greens, Bloom Pop, Bloom Energy) not to luck but to deep pre-launch consumer understanding — specifically, understanding what consumers want to buy and what gives them an experience that drives repurchase.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Products where repeat purchase is the primary value driver
claims.mechanism: Conviction going into a launch is built from genuine consumer insight; products built on that insight earn repurchase because they solve a real, felt want rather than a founder-projected one.

claims.text: Greg Short decided to abandon a protein soda product he wanted to succeed after observing negative purchase signals — watching consumers in retail stores decline to pick it up and tracking negative social media response — concluding that observable consumer behavior overrides founder desire for a product to work.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: In-market observational data available (retail + social media)
claims.mechanism: Retail pick-up behavior and social media response are observable, real-time signals of consumer demand; when both are negative, they falsify the founder's internal conviction and warrant exit regardless of personal attachment to the idea.
bounded_by: Does not apply when product has not yet reached distribution (no observable in-market data)

examples.text: Greg Short launched and succeeded with three consumer products — Greens, Bloom Pop, and Bloom Energy — which he describes as home runs or grand slams. He attributes each success to deep consumer understanding and conviction built from that understanding, rather than luck. When he subsequently developed a protein soda he personally wanted to work, he watched consumers in retail stores avoid picking it up and tracked social media response, both of which signaled low demand. Despite his personal attachment to the product, he walked away from it — citing his willingness to let observable consumer signals override his founder desire as the disciplined behavior that protected his track record.

practices.text: Before committing to a product launch, watch real consumers interact with the product category in retail environments and monitor social media response; if neither signals purchase intent, walk away regardless of personal conviction about the product.
